M12 connector or cable outlet. Protection IP65 and IP67.</item>
  <item id="pd-001" type="product" source="Synthetic product record" version="1 (2026-09-30)">Pressure transmitter series PT.   <item id="pd-003" type="product" source="Synthetic product record" version="1 (2026-09-30)">Temperature sensor series TS. Pt100 and Pt1000 elements in probe, screw-in and surface versions. Doubt about a product concerns behaviour in the customer's own process: stability over a shift, in dust, through repeated starts.   <item id="pd-007" type="product" source="Synthetic product record" version="1 (2026-09-30)">Photoelectric sensor series OP. Diffuse, retro-reflective and through-beam versions with sensing ranges up to 12 metres. A contamination output signals when dust on the lens reduces the signal reserve. Rated values are laboratory values with clean optics; detection stability in dusty processes depends on cleaning intervals and the chosen signal reserve. Protection IP67. Response time 0.5 milliseconds.</item>
  <item id="pb-022" type="playbook" source="Industrial sensor application practice" version="1 (2026-09-30)">A change to the specification during commercial discussions reopens the technical acceptance. Prices agreed for the earlier specification may not hold for the changed one.</item>

  narrative: Met with Marcus and the engineering team at ValoChem Dynamics today for the tech review on their new polymer extruding line. They are a massive outfit, over 4,000 employees worldwide, and about 85% of these skids are slated for export to manufacturing hubs across Germany and South Korea. Their brand-new facility in Brno is still undergoing paint touch-ups on the second floor. They do not have an incumbent sensor supplier for this line since it is a completely clean-sheet design. Marcus went over the mechanical and thermal spec sheets with us line by line. The core pain point they are battling is signal drift during rapid heat cycles on their prototype rig. Per their engineering document, the sensor head has to run continuously at 150 degrees Celsius. The customer states that this requirement could be revised if there is a good reason. They are in a rush and need to issue the PO immediately for 200 proximity units to hit their commissioning schedule. No pushback or concerns were raised during the call.
</scenario>

Doubt about a supplier concerns whether the company understands the customer's industry and will support it.</item>
  <item id="pb-031" type="playbook" source="Industrial sourcing practice" version="1 (2026-09-30)">Words such as unproven or reliability are used for both kinds of doubt.   <item id="pb-044" type="playbook" source="Account planning practice for machine builders" version="1 (2026-09-30)">Notes in an account file age.   <item id="pb-001" type="playbook" source="Synthetic sales policy" version="1 (2026-09-30)">Discount authority. Sales staff and account managers may approve a discount of up to 5 percent on the quoted price. Any discount above 5 percent needs the approval of the sales director, whatever the order volume and however small the difference. A request for approval states the customer's target price, the annual volume and the conditions that have already been agreed.</item>
  <item id="pb-038" type="playbook" source="General B2B sales practice: negotiation" version="1 (2026-09-30)">A price discussion is productive once technical acceptance, supplier admission and delivery terms are complete. Price agreed while a technical question is open is often renegotiated when the question is answered.</item>
  <item id="pb-045" type="playbook" source="Export machinery practice" version="1 (2026-09-30)">Export-oriented machine builders ship against contractual delivery dates with penalties for delay. A late component delays the whole machine, which is why delivery reliability often weighs more than unit price in their choice of supplier.</item>
  <item id="pb-046" type="playbook" source="Export machinery practice" version="1 (2026-09-30)">Builders who cannot rely on a supplier's delivery dates hold safety stock of critical components. The cost of this stock is a recurring argument for qualifying a second source.</item>
  <item id="pb-005" type="playbook" source="Synthetic sales policy" version="1 (2026-09-30)">Payment and delivery terms. Standard payment term is 30 days net. New customers pay the first order in advance or against a letter of credit. Export deliveries are quoted FCA or CIF. Annual framework agreements fix price and call-off quantities for 12 months.</item>
</knowledge>
<scenario>
  sales_stage: negotiation
  customer_size: medium
  export_oriented: true
  has_incumbent: true
  pain_points: delivery delays
  objections: price reduction of 15 percent
  narrative: Met with Dan from K-Mach, a mid-sized firm exporting 80% of their bottling rigs to Europe. They currently source digital flow sensors from SensoCorp, but delivery delays hurt their build schedule. Technical specs were frozen last month. Dan needs to issue the PO immediately for this quarter's batch. He mentioned their plant AC was acting up today. All other terms are agreed and the buyer requires a price reduction of 15 percent. The customer states that this requirement cannot be changed.
</scenario>
